checks: The group action is a genuine ambient affine map because c is affine, and preserves each fiber measure since a finite-order linear map has determinant of absolute value one. Invariant fiber centroids are fixed by the group and its zero mean forces each centered centroid to be zero.
Ambient depth superlevel sets are convex by the halfspace argument. Orbit averaging takes any deepest mark over the same sampled p to the center over p.

Full affine cap differentiation through a specified deepest mark gives the full section centroid equal to the mark. If another deepest point lies inside, a small positive threshold shift retains it and loses mass. If it is on the plane but distinct, the direction W=Y′−Y through Y′ gives −S‖Y′−Y‖². Positive continuous-normal balance then excludes another deepest point on the same fiber.

The orbit caps have identical centered base tilt and normals A^(−T)u. Regularity and the positive threshold coarea carry over because the group maps preserve the measured cap-mass function under invertible affine parameter changes. The mean inverse transpose is zero. A minimal positive support among the balancing weights has at most d+1 members.

At an exposed vertex maximizing the common tilt, each selected cap contains its parallel through-centroid trace. A large finite affine base penalty localizes the support uniformly over all unit normals. The nonnegative old radial flux there has denominator d|K_e|. The central cut's planar-face flux vanishes, so the captured old boundary flux is d times the central cap volume, also by endpoint subtraction for d=1.

Full-volume centroid depth yields Γ_d on each selected cap separately and hence on every probability mixture. Central symmetry yields exactly half on the parallel central trace, giving the stronger lower bound for each actual trace.
